# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when playing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding aversions and some foods do not agree with her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to walk or sit up than other kids her age, and her movements seem a bit different from her friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay is common.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear once.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to look at things, and her eyes get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes a bit longer to reach some milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's movements seem a bit different from her friends, and she takes a bit longer to reach some milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to investigate potential heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor for spinal or hip issues
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and behaviour.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences breathing difficulties, as evidenced by breathing faster than other kids when playing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when playing, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, with frequent bathroom visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and bowel issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and takes medication for it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear, which was treated with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear is common in individuals with KBG syndrome, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board at school and needs to sit closer.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development is delayed, and they do not talk like other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need special education plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development is delayed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and hip dysplasia, are reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess cardiac issues
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and behaviour
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular review of bowel problems and adjustment of treatment as needed

Parent: His front teeth are quite large compared to the rest. We've been advised to monitor them closely to ensure they don't cause any alignment issues or affect his bite.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says he needs regular heart check-ups due to a pre-existing condition. So far‚ everything has been stable‚ but we have to be vigilant about his heart health.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ yes... He falls more often than other children his age. We're working on improving his balance and coordination through physical therapy.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, seeming to hear some sounds but not others clearly, and has undergone testing to understand the extent of the issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, struggling to see things clearly, especially when they're far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to the rest, requiring close monitoring to ensure they don't cause alignment issues or affect his bite.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind other children in development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many requiring special educational support.

* Consideration of a palate review if feeding or speech concerns arise.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition that requires regular check-ups to monitor everything.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with feeding and has had to adapt her diet to ensure she can eat comfortably and safely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including taking longer to reach certain milestones like walking and sitting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sensitive to noise and gets frustrated easily in loud environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness) and needs special glasses to correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with chewing and managing harder foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and is sensitive to noise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a late-closing fontanelle, which is being monitored by doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curved 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Check position of testes in boys
* Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns)
* Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, which is a heart condition that may require monitoring or treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences issues with bowel movements, having difficulty with regular bowel movements without straining.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and gastrointestinal issues are common in people with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't respond for a few seconds, and has a history of speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and around 20-40% experience seizures. Additionally, many have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV up really high, which may indicate hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV when watching her favorite shows or reading books, which may indicate vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of sensitive teeth when eating cold foods and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel and may experience a variety of dental concerns, including large front teeth.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient started talking later than other kids her age and sometimes struggles to find the right words.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many require special educational support.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't respond for a few seconds, and has a history of speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience short fingers and curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to assess for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint

* Referral for speech therapy to address speech delay and difficulties

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to keep up with peers during playtime and gets winded easily, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had significant feeding difficulties as an infant, including trouble latching onto breast or bottle feeding and spitting up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, struggles with balance and precise movements, and sometimes trips over his own feet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have difficulties with coordination and balance.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and tends to turn the volume of the TV up very high to hear it properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision and is hesitant to wear glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing, especially with harder foods, and has noticeably short fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably short fingers and had undescended testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers and curved 5th fingers.

* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Check position of testes in boys

* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis

* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs his eyes, especially when trying to focus on something, indicating potential vision problems.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal health
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any concerns.
